indication: 慢性冠症候群 (Chronic Coronary Syndrome)

similar_trials.population: CCS patients with previous coronary stent requiring long-term OAC
similar_trials.primary_endpoint: Composite: CV death, MI, stroke, systemic embolism, coronary revascularization, acute limb ischemia
similar_trials.key_findings: Aspirin increased CV events, mortality, and major bleeding

similar_trials.population: Stable atherosclerotic vascular disease (CAD or PAD)
similar_trials.primary_endpoint: Composite MACE: CV death, stroke, MI
similar_trials.key_findings: Rivaroxaban + aspirin superior to aspirin alone

similar_trials.population: ACS or high bleeding risk patients undergoing PCI
similar_trials.primary_endpoint: Co-primary: Major bleeding (BARC 3/5) and CV events
similar_trials.key_findings: Prasugrel monotherapy non-inferior for CV events with less bleeding

similar_trials.population: Healthy older adults ≥70 years (≥65 for US minorities)
similar_trials.primary_endpoint: Composite: Death, dementia, persistent physical disability
similar_trials.key_findings: No MACE benefit, increased major hemorrhage (HR 1.24)

regulatory_pathway.rationale: Aspirin is already FDA-approved; new indication/population study would require sNDA
key_requirements: Phase 3 or Phase 4 randomized controlled trial

population_considerations: Define CCS according to ESC/AHA guidelines
study_design_recommendations.follow_up_duration: Minimum 12-24 months for CV event outcomes

key_learnings: Recent AQUATIC trial shows aspirin may increase events in CCS+OAC patients
Bleeding risk is a critical consideration in aspirin trials
MACE composite endpoint is standard for CV outcome trials
Sample sizes of 1000-3000 typical for well-powered CV trials
Early stopping for safety is possible - need robust DSMB
